key_insight: The paper shows that combining interpretable machine learning with data storytelling can make AI decisions understandable to non-experts while still protecting sensitive data.
engineering_relevance: This work offers a practical framework for building explainable AI systems that communicate model behavior through narrative rather than technical plots alone.
method: Defines data storytelling for IML and introduces the DIST Pyramid and I-P-O Model.
Builds an explanation architecture for separate "What-if" and "Why-not" story generation.
Uses data desensitization plus SHAP and LLMs to generate ABT-style narratives.
evidence_signal: In a Boston Housing case study, 76.4% and 74.3% of respondents found the "What-if" and "Why-not" stories more comprehensible, with higher accessibility scores than standard SHAP visualizations.
watch_item: The approach depends on narrative generation and desensitization quality, so preserving explanation fidelity while avoiding leakage of sensitive data or model details remains a key implementation challenge.
paper_title: Data storytelling meets interpretable machine learning: Decoding AI decisions for non-experts without revealing sensitive data and model details
